main_topics.reason: The user opened by asking which RA drugs are compatible with trying for a baby and pregnancy, and several turns covered it.
The user asked for the sequence of steps for trying in 18 months and what happens if the new drug controls RA less well.
The user learned methotrexate must be stopped before conception and asked whether being on it now is a worry, then discussed contraception.
The user and partner hope to try for a baby in 1-2 years, which frames the whole conversation.
The user asked in one turn whether the pregnancy-safe meds are also fine while breastfeeding.
The user asked how RA changes in pregnancy and said they want to be ready for postpartum flares.
The user asked who to coordinate with and whether to raise the plan now, and said they will bring it up at the next visit.
The user said they were scared of having to choose between health and a baby and left feeling relieved.
main_topics.topic: anxiety about health versus having a baby

output.summary: A user recently diagnosed with RA who is on methotrexate wanted to plan medication choices ahead of trying for a baby in 1-2 years. The bot explained compatible and incompatible drugs, contraception, the switch timeline, postpartum flares, breastfeeding and who to coordinate with, then gave a recap. The user said they went from anxious to feeling they had a handle on it and planned to raise it with their rheumatologist.
